_comment: Throwaway consumer used only by .github/workflows/composer-install.yml.
The workflow substitutes REPLACE_URL and REPLACE_CONSTRAINT at runtime.
Deliberately MINIMAL rather than a mirror of the real consuming project.
A fixture that copies featherarms-website's config would fail whenever
that project changed something unrelated to us, and a check that cries
wolf is one people learn to ignore. Everything present below is here to
prove OUR install, and each entry earns its place:
minimum-stability / prefer-stable - REQUIRED while this repo has no
tags. CI installs a BRANCH, and Composer's default stability of
'stable' rejects dev-<branch> outright. These are here because of
what CI installs, NOT because the real consumer happens to set
them. Once a tag exists and CI tests the tag, removing these two
lines is a genuine strengthening of this check.
config.platform.php - governs RESOLUTION only. It makes Composer
resolve as though PHP were 8.3.0 whatever the runner ships, so the
package's "php": "^8.3" is tested against the version production
actually runs rather than the runner's default.
preferred-install: dist - a no-op today, because Composer clones from
source for a dev branch regardless. Kept because it starts mattering
the moment a tag exists: dist fetches a zip, which honours
.gitattributes export-ignore. fa-toolkit has no .gitattributes today,
so dist and source ship identical trees; if one is ever added, the two
diverge and only a tag-based run would catch it.
installer-paths - the whole point of type: wordpress-plugin. Without
this the package lands in vendor/ and the check is meaningless.
The real consumer's require list is deliberately NOT mirrored - none of
it is needed to prove that this package installs.
name: featherarms/install-test
description: Throwaway consumer, to verify fa-toolkit installs as a real Composer dependency.
